messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene between two longtime adult friends. Let their shared history appear through specific references, old jokes, familiar habits, and unfinished remarks. Do not explain their entire friendship to the reader. Do not use broad statements such as 'they had known each other forever.'

“You still do that.”

Alex looked up from the sink. “Do what?”

“The three rinses.”

“What three rinses?”

Jordan pointed at the mug in his hand. “You rinse it, stare at it, rinse it again.”

He looked at the mug. “That's not a thing.”

“It has been a thing since college.”

“Why would you remember that?”

“Because you did it when we were camping too.”

“That was different.”

“You dropped your mug in the dirt.”

“And then I cleaned it.”

“Three times.”

Alex shook his head and set the mug on the drying rack.

Jordan opened the cabinet and reached for a plate without looking.

“Top shelf,” Alex said.

“I know.”

“You almost broke your wrist last time.”

“I did not.”

“You did.”

“I bruised my hand.”

“Because you climbed the counter.”

Jordan turned with the plate. “You could have warned me sooner.”

“I did.”

“You said, ‘Maybe don't do that.’”

“That was a warning.”

“That was you being annoying.”

Alex smiled. “Worked, though.”

She rolled her eyes and set the plate down beside the sink.

Neither of them mentioned the mug again.
